title: Grothendieck existence: a compatible system of modules over the thickenings comes from a finitely presented flat module with proper support
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-existence the theorem asserts the existence of a finitely presented O_X-module F, flat over A and with support proper over A, whose reductions F_n agree with the given system compatibly with the maps phi_n (statement lines 8318-8326). The proof assembles the module first: Lemmas labelled lemma-compute-what-it-should-be, lemma-compute-against-perfect, lemma-relative-pseudo-coherence, lemma-compute-over-affine, lemma-finitely-presented and lemma-proper-support together produce an open subscheme W of X containing all points lying over Spec(A_n) and a finitely presented O_W-module F whose support is proper over A with F_n = F otimes O_{X_n} for all n (proof lines 8328-8338). Lemma labelled lemma-proper-pure then shows F is universally pure relative to Spec(A), so Theorem labelled theorem-flat-dimension-n-representable, explained by Lemma labelled lemma-when-universal-flattening, gives a universal flattening S' -> Spec(A) which is a monomorphism of finite presentation (proof lines 8340-8346). Since the base change of F to Spec(A_n) is F_n, each Spec(A_n) -> Spec(A) factors uniquely through S', and Lemma labelled lemma-monomorphism-isomorphism forces S' = Spec(A), which means F is flat over A (proof lines 8348-8354). Finally the scheme theoretic support Z of F is proper over Spec(A), hence Z -> X is closed, so the pushforward of F along W -> X has all the desired properties (proof lines 8356-8358). Turning the formal existence of the module into flatness through the universal flattening and the monomorphism criterion is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
